analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Lower oil prices and rising stock markets ahead of the US election
key_insights: US equities fell initially on Friday evening but recovered to roughly the levels at the European close. AI-related concerns were the main driver, with the Nasdaq down almost 3% and the S&P 500 down just under 2%.
Risk appetite returned over the weekend. Equity futures in the US and Europe point higher and Asian stock markets are rising.
Trump said he wants to give diplomacy another chance in the Middle East. Oil fell almost USD 4 per barrel, reversing last week's increase, and Brent trades just under USD 110.

Market expectations for central bank rate hikes declined last week despite higher oil prices. SEB cites slightly less hawkish central banks and unchanged policy rates in October as probably more important than petrol and diesel prices not rising (petrol prices in particular have fallen).
The France-Germany yield spread has started to widen again after narrowing on Moody's decision to leave France's rating unchanged. It remains some way below its peak of 175 basis points.
The US midterm elections on Tuesday are the main focus of the week. A Democratic House majority is widely expected, and Polymarket puts the chance of a Democratic Senate at just over 70%.

If Democrats win both chambers, Trump's ability to implement policy would be constrained, though he keeps considerable influence over trade, immigration and foreign policy. He can also veto almost any legislation lacking two-thirds support in both chambers.

Swedish Q3 growth was strong according to the flash GDP estimate, which SEB calls not always reliable. SEB sees upside revision potential when full figures are published on 27 November, but risks to its growth forecast are tilted to the downside.

Swedish household confidence fell sharply in the NIER survey. Energy prices are expected to rise significantly over the next 3-4 months and Riksbank hikes add pressure on indebted households, so consumption could slow.
SEB's Housing Price Indicator fell 5 points to 38. The level still points to rising house prices, but there is a significant risk of further declines.

SEB expects Swedish CPIF excluding energy at 0.4% y/y in October (from 0.5%), slightly below consensus, and headline CPIF at 1.4% (from 1.5%). Electricity prices are expected to rise significantly in November and December and fuel prices to rise 15% in December on a tax normalisation, taking CPIF to 2.7% y/y in December.

Almost everyone expects the Riksbank to hike on Wednesday. SEB expects the message that the September rate path, which signals just under two more hikes next year, remains valid. Half of respondents in SEB's survey expect a signal that upside risks have increased.
The Swedish Riksdag votes on Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister on Tuesday and she is widely expected to lose. There is no breakthrough in government formation talks.

Norges Bank is widely expected to hold its policy rate at 4.50%. SEB expects emphasis on uncertainty about underlying inflation and the risk that external price pressures slow disinflation, with little new guidance. No new forecasts are published at this interim meeting.

tension_points.bull_case: Flash GDP shows strong Q3 growth, other indicators support it, and SEB sees a possible slight upward revision on 27 November. The housing indicator at 38 still points to rising house prices.
tension_points.bear_case: Household confidence fell sharply in the NIER survey, energy prices are expected to rise significantly over 3-4 months and Riksbank hikes pressure indebted households, so consumption could slow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further deterioration in consumer confidence and a further decline in the housing price indicator in coming months.
